# HubSpot vs ActiveCampaign (2027): CRM-First Suite or Automation-First Email Tool, Prices, Free Plan, Startup Discounts and Which One Fits Your Startup

## HubSpot vs ActiveCampaign: CRM-First Suite or Automation-First Email Tool for Your Startup?

HubSpot and ActiveCampaign both send newsletters, run automated email sequences and keep a contact database, but they start from opposite ends. **HubSpot** is a customer platform built around a free CRM: marketing, sales, service, content and data tools share one contact record, and you add paid hubs as you grow. **ActiveCampaign** is an email marketing and automation tool first, priced by the number of contacts, with a CRM and sales pipeline you can add later. We checked both pricing pages, in their default view, in October 2026.

**Quick answer:** start on **HubSpot's free plan** if you want one free CRM for sales and marketing and send fewer than 2,000 marketing emails a month (with HubSpot branding); its Starter plan costs $7 per seat a month on annual billing as a limited-time offer for new customers. Choose **ActiveCampaign** when email automation is your main growth channel: Starter costs $15 and Plus, with unlimited automation steps and landing pages, $49 a month billed yearly for 1,000 contacts, after a 14-day free trial. HubSpot's unlimited automation needs Marketing Hub Professional, from $800 a month plus a $3,000 onboarding fee.

> **Are you getting customers from ChatGPT yet?**  
>   
> More and more traffic is coming from Perplexity, ChatGPT, Grok and other AI tools.  
>   
> 👉 **[Rank on ChatGPT](https://femaleswitch.com/accelerate-startup-idea)**

## HubSpot vs ActiveCampaign at a Glance

|     | HubSpot (Marketing Hub) | ActiveCampaign |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What it is | Customer platform on a free CRM: Marketing, Sales, Service, Content and Data hubs | Email marketing and marketing automation, with CRM add-ons, SMS and WhatsApp |
| Built for | Teams that want marketing and sales on one contact record | Marketers who live in email sequences, segments and automations |
| Free option | Free plan for up to 2 users, no credit card; 2,000 email sends a month with HubSpot branding | No free plan; 14-day free trial, no credit card; 30-day money-back guarantee |
| Paid plans (annual billing) | Starter $7 per seat a month (limited-time new-customer offer; $20 shown as the regular price); Professional from $800 a month (3 seats); Enterprise from $3,600 a month (5 seats) | Starter $15, Plus $49, Pro $79, Enterprise $145 a month for 1,000 contacts |
| Setup fees | Professional $3,000, Enterprise $7,000 one-time onboarding | None listed |
| Users | Starter priced per seat; 3 seats on Professional, 5 on Enterprise | 1 user on Starter and Plus, 3 on Pro, 5 on Enterprise |
| Contacts and sends | 1,000 marketing contacts on Starter; sends 5x (Starter), 10x (Pro) or 20x (Enterprise) the contact tier a month | Price scales with contacts; sends 10x (Starter, Plus), 12x (Pro) or 15x (Enterprise) the contact limit |
| Automation | 1 automated action (Free), up to 10 (Starter), unlimited and omni-channel (Professional) | 5 actions per automation (Starter), unlimited from Plus; 950+ automation recipes |
| AI  | Breeze AI agents and features paid with HubSpot Credits: 500 (Starter), 3,000 (Pro), 5,000 (Enterprise) | Active Intelligence on every plan with 500 AI credits; generative AI from Plus, predictive sending from Pro |
| Integrations | Over 2,000 apps | 1,000+ integrations, Zapier, Claude and ChatGPT via MCP |
| Startup programme | HubSpot for Startups: up to 90% off Professional or Enterprise in year one | ActiveCampaign Incubator: 90% off any annual plan in year one |

_Sources: hubspot.com marketing and Customer Platform pricing pages and HubSpot for Startups; activecampaign.com pricing and Incubator pages; checked 31 October 2026. Both pages showed USD with annual billing selected by defaul

# HubSpot Marketing Hub vs ActiveCampaign: Testing the Best AI Marketing Tools for Ecommerce

If you subscribe to a service from a link on this page, Reeves and Sons Limited may earn a commission. See our [ethics statement](https://ecommerce-platforms.com/disclosures).

![cat illustration](https://ecommerce-platforms.com/wp-content/themes/ep/assets/images/cat-2.svg)

 [![](//ecommerce-platforms.com/wp-content/plugins/a3-lazy-load/assets/images/lazy_placeholder.gif) Bogdan Rancea Author](https://ecommerce-platforms.com/author/rancea)

[16 min](https://ecommerce-platforms.com/articles/hubspot-marketing-hub-vs-activecampaign) Updated:  [Apr 13, 2026](https://ecommerce-platforms.com/articles/hubspot-marketing-hub-vs-activecampaign)

I’ve been running ecommerce campaigns long enough to know one thing: a CRM can either double your sales or drain your week. When it works, it’s incredible, getting all your leads, emails, and sales data all flowing in one place. When it doesn’t, you’re lost in tabs, chasing follow-ups that slipped through the cracks.

[HubSpot CRM](https://www.hubspot.com/products/crm/what-is) is the one I usually use as a benchmark. It’s just so comprehensive, with all those different hubs for sales, marketing, service, **and even commerce working together**. But ActiveCampaign has its value too, particularly if you want to get real about automating your marketing strategies.

So, which one do you really need? In this review, I’ll break down exactly how each platform handled everything from setup to sales automation, and why, if you’re growing an ecommerce brand, **HubSpot CRM still comes out on top**.

## Quick Comparison Table: HubSpot vs ActiveCampaign

Before diving into the details, here’s the snapshot I wish someone had shown me before I started testing.

| **Feature** | **HubSpot Marketing Hub** | **ActiveCampaign** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Setup & onboarding | Guided onboarding, free CRM ready in minutes, unified workspace | Quick campaign setup, but CRM integration needed for full tracking |
| AI tools | Breeze AI Agents (Content, Social, Prospecting), AI CPQ, Data Hub Intelligence | Predictive Sending, Content Optimization, Active Intelligence agents |
| Marketing automation | Full inbound engine – email, ads, SEO, landing pages, workflows | Strong email automation and branching; solid CRM layering |
| Omnichannel messaging | Email, social, ads, SMS (via integration) | Native email + SMS + WhatsApp + transactional email |
| CRM & pipeline management | Native Smart CRM; pipelines capped by plan | Built-in CRM with unlimited pipelines on all plans |
| Reporting & analytics | Multi-touch attribution, custom dashboards, Data Hub warehouse integration | Campaign-level analytics; excellent for email flows, limited cross-channel view |
| Integrations & ecosystem | 2,000 apps; deep two-way data sync (Shopify, Slack, Stripe etc.) | 1,000 apps; good email integrations, heavier reliance on Zapier |
| Pricing & cost | Free CRM, tiered hubs (users + features) | Contact-based pricing; cheaper start but scales fast |
| Onboarding & support | HubSpot Academy, docs, partner network, optional paid migration | Free 1:1 migration (Pro +), good support for email teams |
| Deliverability & localization | Strong deliverability; web content translation via DeepL | Excellent deliverability; native support for 75 languages |
| Best for | Growing ecommerce or B2B brands needing unified data + automation | Email-driven teams needing fast, powerful flows on a budget |

## HubSpot vs ActiveCampaign: What Each Platform Is Really Built For

Ok, so both tools are CRM products, but with very different definitions. [HubSpot Marketing Hub](https://www.hubspot.com/marketing/free/em037?utm_id=606912907626&utm_term=marketing_hubspot%20marketing%20hub_EN&utm_campaign=Marketing_Portals_EN_EMEA_UKI_Brand_e_c_campaignid13467922781_agid120265675621_google&utm_source=google&utm_medium=paid&utm_content=_&hsa_acc=9694350438&hsa_cam=13467922781&hsa_grp=120265675621&hsa_ad=606912907626&hsa_src=g&hsa_tgt=kwd-676600522284&hsa_kw=hubspot%20marketing%20hub&hsa_mt=e&hsa_net=adwords&hsa_ver=3&cq_cmp=13467922781&cq_plac=&cq_net=g&gad_source=1&gad_campaignid=13467922781&gbraid=0AAAAADP5F9yTuckgGDgy4m2nehLzo1M2E&gclid=Cj0KCQjwmYzIBhC6ARIsAHA3IkSlEKjBXLaQJc_JMgmlMHaC8-G5bqQVknC1lP5TbCck9qtfHn3Yw9MaAlhfEALw_wcB) is part of HubSpot’s complete smart CRM ecosystem. Everything’s built to work in one place: your emails, your ads, your deals, even payments.

The beauty of that setup is what happens behind the scenes. When someone fills out a form, **HubSpot logs it**, scores the lead, and triggers a workflow, maybe an email, **maybe a task for your sales rep**.

![hubspot marketing hub homepage](//ecommerce-platforms.com/wp-content/plugins/a3-lazy-load/assets/images/lazy_placeholder.gif)

The data flows automatically. Add in [Breeze AI](https://www.hubspot.com/products/artificial-intelligence), and suddenly the system isn’t just tracking activity; it’s helping you act on it. For ecommerce, that means one clear timeline from first ad click to checkout.

ActiveCampaign has a different energy. It’s fast, it’s focused, and it’s unapologetically built for marketing people. Particularly marketing automation people invested in email. You can spin up a campaign, **drop in conditions, and start firing personalized automations in less than an hour**.

![activecampaign homepage](//ecommerce-platforms.com/wp-content/plugins/a3-lazy-load/assets/images/lazy_placeholder.gif)

It shines when timing is everything: things like post-purchase follow-ups, nurture sequences, and high-frequency offers. The Predictive Sending and Active Intelligence tools are genuinely clever, and they’ve improved a lot in 2025.

## Getting Started: Setup & Ease of Use

Getting started with new CRM software can go either way. Some tools make you feel like you’re climbing a wall of settings before you even send your first email. **Others guide you just enough to make things click**.

Getting started with HubSpot doesn’t feel like setup in the traditional sense. You open a free account, plug in your store, maybe your email and ad tools too, and the system just starts pulling things together.

![hubspot marketing hub ease of use](//ecommerce-platforms.com/wp-content/plugins/a3-lazy-load/assets/images/lazy_placeholder.gif)
